parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim and does mean what the objector says: v(B) was defined (Section 4) as the nested difference taken in the *decreasing* order b_1≥…≥b_r, and the strategy then processes b_2,…,b_r 'in turn', i.e. in that order. But the proof of Theorem 4.2 only produces, via Lemma 4.1, *some* ordering of P∪N whose nested difference equals g; it never shows the decreasing order attains it. Decreasing order is not optimal in general: for {8,7,6,5,4} the decreasing nested value is ||||8-7|-6|-5|-4| = 4, while the ordering 8,4,6,7,5 gives 0. So the inference 'Theorem 4.2 ⇒ v(B) (decreasing) ≤ T_n' does not follow. Not fatal: the running-value procedure, cut count, distinctness and parity cancellation are all order-agnostic, so processing B in the ordering Lemma 4.1 already constructs repairs the step verbatim.
